notes: SHIP v1.14.420 - P2 OF PHASE-ENGINE: THE BLOCKER RECORD, WHICH ADOPTS THE BLOCKERS YOU ALREADY HAVE. No UI surface. WHAT A BLOCKER WAS. Three fields ON a phase - blockerNote, blockedAt, status blocked. That cannot satisfy spec section 6.2, which says a BLOCKED step REQUIRES a blockerId referencing a Blocker record: a note has no identity, so nothing can reference it, and Shift section 9.2 must render blockers with descriptions rather than bare counts. Spec section 6.4 defines the record, and the add-nothing rule names it as one of exactly three permitted data additions. THE TRAP THIS SHIP EXISTS TO AVOID. Section 6.2 also says a blocked step with no blocker record is an INVALID state whose transition must be rejected. Enforcing that on a device that already has blocked phases would retroactively declare every blocker the operator has already logged to be illegal - their notes still on disk, their phases still blocked, and the app now calling that state invalid. So migration runs FIRST, at boot, before any surface can assert the invariant, and ADOPTS what is already there: every blocked phase without a blockerId gets a record synthesised from its own note and timestamp. THE NOTE BECOMES THE DESCRIPTION IT ALWAYS WAS. Nothing is invented and nothing is discarded - the original blockerNote stays on the phase untouched, and a blocker with no note gets a record that SAYS no description was recorded rather than fabricating one. A migrated blocker is never attributed to whoever happens to be holding the device now; openedBy reads Unknown pre-v1.14.420, because crediting an old blocker to the current operator would be a quiet lie about who found it. ORDERING IS THE GUARANTEE. On the live path the record is created BEFORE the phase moves to blocked, so the invalid state never exists on disk - not even between two writes. If the record cannot be written, the phase does not move. CLEARING CLOSES, IT DOES NOT DELETE. clear() records who cleared it and when, and the record survives; clearing twice or clearing an unknown id returns null rather than silently succeeding. Open blockers are what the next technician inherits, so the store is REGISTERED for backup - a key that is not in the registry is reported as an unclassified gap and never travels in a backup, which for open blockers would mean the next tech inherits nothing. TESTS: new spec 12-blockers.spec.js, eight tests, all green. The one that matters is the first: a pre-existing blocker is adopted with its note intact, its original timestamp preserved, and its phase now referencing the record instead of being an illegal state. Also pinned: migration is idempotent and never duplicates; a note-less blocker says so honestly; opening through the real door credits the profile actor and writes a BLOCKER_OPENED v2 event carrying the rack; and the new store is classified for backup. GATES: 3 inline blocks compile, node --check sw.js, valid JSON, braces balanced, CRLF intact, three-stamp lockstep, enforced by the commit hook. No RACK SCENE LOCK term touched. ?legacy=1 unaffected. DEVICE-VERIFY: no visible surface. Confirm v1.14.420, then confirm any blockers you already had are still listed with their original notes. In the console, PHANTOM_BLOCKERS.open() should list them, each with the description you wrote and openedBy reading Unknown pre-v1.14.420 - that is the migration being honest about what it does not know, not data loss.
